title: Google Health API
notes: sha256 and byteLength describe spec/v4/discovery.json exactly as committed.

The snapshot is stored CANONICALIZED: object keys sorted ordinally, 2-space indent, LF, UTF-8 without BOM, trailing newline. Array order, numbers and strings are preserved exactly, so the content is identical to the endpoint response.

Canonicalization is required, not cosmetic. Verified 2026-08-09: the Discovery endpoint returns randomized object key order on every request. Four consecutive fetches gave four different SHA-256 values at an identical byte length with no semantic difference. Storing the raw response would make the recorded hash meaningless, and would render every specification update as a whole-file diff instead of a reviewable contract change.
Never hand-edit this file and never paste in a raw endpoint response. Use: codegen fetch --version v4
See .gitattributes: the snapshot is stored with -text so no line-ending rewriting occurs.
retrievedAtUtc is provenance only and must never reach generated C#.
